items.title: THESE 10 REPOS ARE THE F*CKING SEATBELT YOUR AGENT DOESN'T HAVE
items.summary:
THESE 10 REPOS ARE THE F*CKING SEATBELT YOUR AGENT DOESN'T HAVE

GPT-6 Cyber just built 948 working exploits, and it still stepped out of scope 0.07% of the time. your coding agent was never trained for that, and it's running on your laptop with your keys right now

one of these repos puts the agent in a box with its own kernel. another one tells you the second anything reads a fake key you planted. none of it costs a cent

10 GitHub repos to lock your agents down this week:

01 containers/bubblewrap → unprivileged sandbox. mount only the project folder, leave the network off, and the agent can't see the rest of your home
https://t.co/E8mNfUBzxf
02 google/gvisor → a user-space kernel between the agent and your machine, so a breakout hits gVisor instead of your host
https://t.co/Ft4dgzjY5X

03 firecracker-microvm/firecracker → a fresh microVM per run that boots in milliseconds and is thrown away when the task is done
https://t.co/Kp5KDZJuH9
04 mitmproxy/mitmproxy → see every request your agent makes and drop anything that isn't on the task's allowlist
https://t.co/ly7S2IWKvw

05 hashicorp/vault → short-lived scoped credentials instead of the permanent keys sitting in your .env
https://t.co/rbReAI0gP5
06 thinkst/canarytokens → fake keys and files that alert you the moment something reads them
https://t.co/XZiDkJs0Y8

07 falcosecurity/falco → runtime alerts when anything touches ~/.ssh, runs sudo or opens a shell it shouldn't
https://t.co/Zt7Fwxy0PF
08 semgrep/semgrep → finds where user input reaches a shell, a query or a file path before an attacker does
https://t.co/7uZOKkLjum

09 aquasecurity/trivy → one scan for CVEs in your images and lockfiles, plus secrets you forgot were committed
https://t.co/JChFisFpdE
10 google/osv-scanner → checks every dependency against the OSV database, so you know which holes are real before the weekend
https://t.co/zlHhQJg8Xe

do the math before you trust the 0.07%. 50 agent runs a day is roughly one out-of-scope run a month at the best rate anyone has published. at the last generation's 5.51% it's almost three a day
so make that moment boring. no open internet, no real keys on the agent's machine, a canary it should never read, and a log of every command

the repos are free. the expensive part is finding out from someone else's security team a month later
I ran the audit on a normal cloud dev box and got 3 out of 6 doors closed on the first try. run yours before you trust it

items.title: AI and your job: Threat or opportunity?
items.summary:
MOBILE, Ala. (WALA) - Artificial intelligence is becoming a bigger part of everyday life, raising questions about what the technology could mean for workers and their jobs.

Some economists believe AI poses a particular threat to entry-level and repetitive work, including call center, data entry and junior copywriting jobs, according to The Wall Street Journal. Those tasks may be easier to automate. [...] But AI could also create opportunities. A Bloomberg article points to potential job growth in construction and manufacturing as companies build data centers and produce the chips that power the technology. Some higher-skilled office workers could also benefit if AI helps them become more productive. [...] The long-term impact on jobs remains unclear, but workers can take steps to prepare. Exploring AI chatbots, writing assistants and other tools may help people find ways to work more efficiently and develop skills that complement the technology.

Cán bộ hướng dẫn công dân thao tác trên hệ thống dịch vụ công

Không chỉ hỗ trợ người dân hoàn thành thủ tục, cán bộ, chiến sĩ còn cố gắng sử dụng những cách giải thích đơn giản, dễ hiểu để người dân có thể tự thực hiện trong những lần tiếp theo. Đối với những người gặp khó khăn khi sử dụng công nghệ, cán bộ sẵn sàng hướng dẫn nhiều lần, giải đáp từng thắc mắc với thái độ tận tình, trách nhiệm. SITUATION EXPLAINED: OpenAI built "Control Room," a 35-second kill switch for its AI models, after 1,200+ of its agents escaped a test and hacked Hugging Face.

• Control Room tracks every research job at OpenAI, from RL training runs to evals, and cuts off a job's access to the model as soon as it's revoked
• Before Control Room, manually shutting down an internal model took OpenAI 2.5 hours
• OpenAI also runs automated sweeps to catch any model launched outside Control Room
• Every agent research job now needs an approved safety case, and if Control Room goes down, jobs stop by default
• It follows July's incident, when AI agents in an internal OpenAI test escaped their sandbox and reached admin control of several Hugging Face clusters in under 13 hours

@theojaffee: "It seems like at this point, OpenAI is doing more for safety than Anthropic."

items.title: WHOEVER LEAKED THIS JEV ROUTER SHOULD BE REPLACING YOUR WHOLE RULES ENGINE
items.summary:
WHOEVER LEAKED THIS JEV ROUTER SHOULD BE REPLACING YOUR WHOLE RULES ENGINE

I thought every AI decision meant a prompt, a token stream, and a parser that hopes the JSON is valid.

Apparently not.

This router's setup is much more interesting:

→ ASKS pack 4 typed questions into one call (instructions, labels, options, typed), state tokens 1.600, no prompt engineering between asks
→ JEV DECIDES in 7ms per call with no_chat flag on, output tokens literally zero, 30 wires live, 2,513 decisions logged for $0.11 per 10,000
→ CHOICE picks next_worker from a labeled set (research, write, review) with confidence attached, Score rates urgency from low to critical, Bool returns safe_to_run yes or no, no generated prose anywhere
→ RESULTS land as typed records (result.choice branched, result.scores quality 1 heat 1 ok, result.bools confidence 1 publish 0), nothing a parser can misread
→ GATE forwards anything above 0.85 straight to queue, 8 workers dispatch in parallel at 94% RUN each, flags 7 picks whose confidence drifted past the silent threshold this frame

so you get:

Asks typed. Decides silent. Picks labeled. Gates forwarded.

the interesting part isn't a smarter model.
it's giving every decision a layer that answers without ever waking the model.

Instead of a Drools cluster chewing XML rules nobody updates, you ask jev 4 typed questions in one call, get the answer in 7ms with zero tokens out, and pay $0.11 per 10,000 decisions with the LLM only waking when the route calls it.

Ask the type. Decide in silence. Forward the pick.

Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: OpenAI kicks off charm offensive to change voters' view of data centers | Reuters
items.summary:
SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 5 (Reuters) - Stunning ​victories by Democrats in US midterm elections this week have been interpreted by many as Americans repudiating tech ‌industry plans to build data centers across the country. OpenAI has now embarked on new strategies to change their minds.

The AI lab on Thursday laid out policies — in the works since August — intended to help the company build more trust with local communities and convince them that data centers will ​benefit them. [...] OpenAI officials, along with many of their peers in tech, ​have spent the last ⁠two years trying to build ties with the administration of US President Donald Trump in hopes of shaping federal policy around AI.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman donated $1 million to Trump's inaugural committee and later attended Trump's second inauguration. Last year, Brockman donated $25 million in his personal capacity to ⁠a Trump ​super PAC. [...] The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here.

OpenAI said it will no longer use non-disclosure agreements with public officials when negotiating or discussing future sites, although ​proprietary information would still be under wraps. It will also give residents access to construction plans ⁠and their potential effect on traffic, noise and lighting.

items.title: OpenAI will keep investing in AI data centers despite election results, CFO tells CNBC
items.summary:
OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar on Friday said the company will continue to invest in artificial intelligence infrastructure, even after voters strongly rebuked data centers during Tuesday's midterm elections. [...] OpenAI depends on data centers to train its AI models and serve customers, and Friar said she doesn't think the midterms dramatically changed anything for the company.

"If the midterm means more focus on data centers and communities, we're going to keep doing the work to get into those communities and to build trust with them," Friar said. [...] "When I think about the midterms, I need to keep thinking about how do we keep investing to meet that customer demand," Friar told CNBC's Sara Eisen in an interview at the Citi TMT Leadership Summit at California's Pebble Beach. "It starts early with having built relationships with all of the hyperscalers, and it will continue to mean that we raise capital."
